$comment: Gate 4A.1 — every (nodeType, accessor, name) the C# extractor reads must EXIST in the
vendored grammar's src/node-types.json. Checked before any row is produced.
This exists because childForFieldName('parameters') is CORRECT on method_declaration
(a real field) and SILENTLY NULL on class_declaration (where the parameter list is a
child, not a field). The call sites look identical. The consequence was 0 primary
constructors counted in a .NET 8 reference app, and 173 generic types against 19,567
classes. Both were caught by implausibility rather than by a test.
accessor is 'field' for childForFieldName(name), or 'child' for a named child of that type.
SEMANTICS: node-types.json PARTITIONS a node's contents into fields vs children, but the
parse tree exposes a field-bound node as a named child as well. So accessor 'child' is
satisfied by children.types OR by the type of any field. Checking only children.types is
too strict and produced a false positive on the first run of this gate.

mustFail.name: parameters
mustFail.why: the original defect — primary constructors counted 0

mustFail.name: type_parameters
mustFail.why: the original defect — generic arity always 0, and arity is in the primary key

implementationNote.title: the grammar is INCONSISTENT across sibling type declarations — read arity as a CHILD
detail: interface_declaration binds type_parameters as a FIELD.
class_declaration, struct_declaration and record_declaration do NOT — for those the
type parameter list is only a named child of type type_parameter_list.
So childForFieldName('type_parameters') works for interfaces and is silently null for
classes, structs and records. An extractor that treats type declarations uniformly must
scan for the CHILD type_parameter_list, which works for all five kinds.
